instruction.text: In which book would you find the following quote?

atoms.a: "Luckily, Finn McCool’s wife Oonagh was a very clever woman."
"As the molten rock hit the surface, it began cooling very quickly."
"This boot and the other rocks along the coastline reaching into the water are the last witnesses to the giant’s legendary rivalry."
"The distance between these two locations shows just how powerful the volcanic eruption must have been."

atoms.b: The Giant’s Causeway is a famous ((++rock word)) formation in Northern Ireland. Several explanations have been offered over the years for its ((++creation destruction)), but what is widely agreed upon is that the causeway was formed long, long ago.

Made out of more than 40,000 ((++hexagonal-shaped horizontal-shaped)) columns of rock, the Giant’s Causeway’s impressive landscape sparked not only myths and legends, but also ((++scientific spiritual)) research.
This unique rock formation can be found not only on Northern Ireland’s coastline, but also on an island in ((++Scotland England)) — the Isle of Staffa.

On the one hand, scientists trace the creation of the rock columns back to a massive ((++volcanic_eruption volcanic_rivalry)) several million years ago. The fact that the same rock formations can be found in ((++two four)) locations hundreds of miles apart from each other proves how ((++powerful weak)) this eruption must have been.

On the other hand, Irish and Scottish ((++myths gossip)) explain this magical landscape and its mysterious connection between the land masses through the rivalry of two ((++giants friends)): Finn McCool from Northern Ireland and Benandonner from Scotland. In an attempt to confront the other giant and prove who was stronger, ((++Finn_McCool Oonagh)) built the Giant’s Causeway.
Although the scientific ((++explanation conquest)) might be more accurate, the legend of the rivalry of the two giants might hold some truth to it too.
